subject.title: Proposal: safer self-update with pre-update backup + health check + auto-rollback/restore

question: Should OpenClaw core own an integrated opt-in safe-update transaction that snapshots state, runs real post-update checks, and restores or rolls back on failure?
rationale: The remaining work defines core updater scope, restore semantics, retention policy, secret handling, smoke-check criteria, and coordination with several narrower update/backup issues; automation cannot safely choose those product and security boundaries.

options.title: Sponsor Scoped Core Safe Update
options.body: Define a default-off core updater mode and split implementation into reviewed pieces for snapshots, retention, health/smoke checks, and restore/rollback policy.

options.title: Split Into Narrower Canonicals
options.body: Use the open backup/restore, scanner, auto-update, and external-updater issues as the implementation tracks and keep this issue as an umbrella reference.

options.title: Keep Outside Core For Now
options.body: Document the community workaround and manual recovery flow while declining automatic restore/rollback until updater architecture changes.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Scoped Core Safe Update
recommendation.body: Define a default-off core updater mode and split implementation into reviewed pieces for snapshots, retention, health/smoke checks, and restore/rollback policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest observed connection across the prior keep-open review and the original core updater feature history.
